patches.reason: The shared clothing-image helper returns "swipsuitF.png" for a female swimsuit; the package ships images/Bclothes/swimsuitF.png, and the male entries next to it (speedosM.png, shortsM.png) are spelled correctly. Fix the misspelled file name.

ChooseDeck listed the subfolders of images/Bcards with eachFile and isDirectory() to offer the card decks; TeaseScript cannot list folders, and the folder-listing rule only finds images by their folder's tag. DeckNames is the list of the deck folders the package holds.

Settings the rules menu turns off and saves come back on at the next start: they are read as loadBoolean(key) ?: true, and Groovy elvis treats a saved false like a missing value. Read the saved value, and take true only where nothing is saved.

Two author errors. The female bikini top image is chosen when the clothes name contains "bikini" and no "top", so "bikini top" fell through to the bikini bottom image: test that the name contains "top". Chemin de fer accepts 0 or fewer decks and saves them under Baccarat.NoDecks, which both scripts read, so every later deal of either script failed on an empty shoe: replace them with six, as Baccarat.groovy does at the same question.

Legacy bug (creator report): both Baccarat and Chemin de fer take any number of decks the player types and build the shoe from it (52 cards per deck), so a huge number, such as 111,111,111 decks, made Groovy build 5.8 billion cards and TeaseScript stop (TSR037 at Baccarat.tease:302 and Baccarat-chemin-de-fer.tease:145, V2 explorer). The script says the game is usually played with six decks, and real Baccarat uses up to eight: ask again until the number is 1 to 8, in place of the earlier replacement of 0 or fewer by six.
